privacy.title: Program Partner Privacy Policy
privacy.name: Privacy
meta: Operator: Program Partner, LLC · Contact: support@myprogrampartner.com

segs.text: This Privacy Policy explains how Program Partner, LLC (“Program Partner,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, discloses, protects, retains, and deletes information when schools, arts programs, directors, staff, students, parents, guardians, and other authorized users access the Program Partner web application and related services (the “Services”), and when anyone visits our website at myprogrampartner.com. A mailing address is available upon verified request.

Program Partner is a multi-organization, role-based platform for band, choir, orchestra, theatre, private-studio, and related program-management activities. Enabled features may include communications, calendars, forms, fees and receipt review, fundraising credits, purchase requests, practice logs, Skill Pathways, achievements, inventory, file submissions, and administrative reporting.

For records supplied by or maintained on behalf of a participating school or program, that organization determines the educational or program purpose and controls those records. Program Partner acts as a service provider performing authorized functions. Individual users may separately control limited information associated with their own login account. This distinction affects who may request access, correction, export, or deletion.
Account and identity information.

Names, email addresses, optional phone numbers, account identifiers, authentication method, role assignments, organization memberships, invitation and join-code records, and information needed to connect an authorized parent, guardian, student, director, staff member, or platform administrator to the correct program records.
Google sign-in.

If you sign in with Google, Google provides only your name, email address, and profile picture, which we use to create and identify your account. Program Partner’s use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
School and program records.

Student names, photos, and contact information; ensemble, class, instrument, cast, group, and roster information; guardian and student relationships; participation and attendance-related information; forms, permissions, acknowledgments, and responses; and related timestamps and status records. Forms a program assigns may ask for health and emergency information, such as allergies, medications, physician, and insurance details. When someone signs a form, we record the signature, the signer’s name, the time, and the signer’s IP address and browser. Equipment agreements record the signer’s name, email, typed signature, and the time.
Instructional and progress information.

Practice requirements and logs, Skill Pathways assignments and progress, quizzes, recordings, performance or skills submissions, teacher or director feedback, approvals, achievements, and similar educational records when an organization enables those features.
Inventory, fee, and transaction records.

Equipment and inventory assignments, condition and return records, amounts assigned, balances, credits, payment status, fundraising allocations, purchase requests, receipt images, and records documenting program transactions. When a program enables online payment, card details are entered on the hosted checkout pages of the program’s own payment processor (Stripe, Square, or PayPal), and full card numbers are never stored by Program Partner. Users should not enter full payment-card numbers or other payment credentials into ordinary forms or messages.
Content and files.
Documents, images, audio, video, receipts, form responses, messages, and other content uploaded or submitted through an enabled feature.
Communications and delivery information.

Recipient addresses, message content, portal notifications, email delivery events, bounces, complaints, unsubscribes, and open or click signals where supported. Email privacy tools, image proxies, and link scanners may make engagement signals incomplete or inaccurate.
Calendar and integration information.

Events from a Google or Outlook calendar a program connects (read-only), and Skill Pathways recordings stored in a program’s own Google Drive when it connects one, together with the connection settings and synchronization details needed to provide that integration.
Technical and usage information.

Device and browser information, IP address, session and authentication records, security and audit logs, feature activity, error information, request metadata, and similar operational information used to provide, secure, diagnose, and improve the Services.

items.text: Provide organization-authorized administrative, instructional, communication, transaction, and family-facing workflows.
Authenticate users, connect accounts to appropriate records, and apply organization-, relationship-, and role-based access controls.
Send transactional and program communications, process delivery events, and present message status to authorized users.
Maintain records, provide support, diagnose errors, prevent misuse, investigate incidents, and protect the security and reliability of the Services.
Improve functionality using aggregated or de-identified information where reasonably practicable and consistent with school instructions and applicable law.
Meet legal obligations and enforce agreements governing the Services.

segs.text: Program Partner does not sell personal information. Student information is not used for behavioral advertising, targeted advertising, unrelated profiling, or unrelated commercial purposes. Program Partner will not build advertising profiles from school-controlled records.

The Program Partner app does not send school-controlled records to artificial-intelligence services, and does not let AI assistants or other outside apps sign in to or act on a user’s account. A signed-in user can choose to add a personal calendar subscription link to a calendar app such as Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. That app then receives the events available to the account (for a family, the events it can see; for staff, the organization’s calendar), including titles, times, locations or meeting links, descriptions, cancellation status, and event identifiers.

Program Partner’s developers use AI-assisted coding and code-review tools on the source code and on demonstration data, and do not use them to look at school-controlled records. Older development notes that held limited details about individual users remain in the source code repository’s private history, which those tools can read.

blocks.text: 4. School-authorized use; FERPA and children’s privacy

segs.text: When a school provides education records under an applicable FERPA exception, Program Partner will use those records only to perform the school-authorized service or function, remain subject to the school’s direction and control regarding use and maintenance of the records, and not redisclose or repurpose them except as directed by the school or permitted by law.

For a child under 13, a school may authorize collection on a parent’s behalf only for a school-authorized educational purpose and not for an unrelated commercial purpose. When school authorization is unavailable or insufficient, Program Partner may require verifiable parental consent or decline to collect the information. Participating organizations remain responsible for determining the legal basis for their use, providing required notices, and obtaining any consent required by their policies or applicable law.

Program Partner seeks to collect and retain only information reasonably necessary for an enabled educational or program purpose. This policy does not, by itself, certify compliance with every federal, state, local, or district requirement. Program Partner will cooperate with reasonable privacy reviews and written data-protection terms.

items.text: To authorized users within the participating organization, according to their roles, guardian or student relationships, and legitimate program responsibilities.

To service providers that support hosting, database, authentication, storage, email and text-message delivery, payment processing, security, networking, diagnostics, source control, or related operations, only as needed to provide the Services and subject to appropriate restrictions.
At the direction of the school or program, including approved exports, integrations, transfers, or disclosures initiated by an authorized organization administrator.
To comply with law, legal process, or a valid governmental request; protect rights, safety, or security; investigate misuse; or enforce applicable agreements.
As part of a reorganization, financing, merger, acquisition, or transfer of the business, subject to continued protection of the information and any required notice, consent, or school approval.

segs.text: The following list reflects the current production architecture.

head: Provider
Function
Information processed
rows: Supabase
Database, sign-in, private file storage, scheduled jobs, and APIs, in a Supabase project that Lovable manages for Program Partner (Lovable Cloud), with Lovable Cloud’s own daily backups
Account, school and program, uploaded-file, transaction, communication-status, and technical records
Lovable
Builds and publishes the application and manages its Supabase project (Lovable Cloud); sends sign-in emails; relays outgoing email, text messages, and calendar requests to Resend, Twilio, and Google

Deployment information, browser requests and network metadata, the content of the sign-in emails it sends and of the email, text messages, and calendar requests it relays, and the calendar lists and events returned through it
Cloudflare
Hosts and runs the application (Cloudflare Workers); domain name, network, and security services; website analytics for myprogrampartner.com (see section 12)

The information the app handles as requests pass through it, plus IP address, request headers, security signals, and related network metadata. The application keeps no database on Cloudflare, and its request logs are kept up to 7 days. Cloudflare R2 also stores the encrypted backups (below).
Resend
Delivery of program and notification email, and delivery events
Recipient name and address, message content, message identifiers, and delivery and engagement events
Twilio
Text-message (SMS) delivery for programs that turn it on, including consent and reply handling
Recipient phone number, message content, consent status, and delivery events
Stripe
Card payment processing on Stripe-hosted checkout pages, using each participating program’s own Stripe account

Program Partner sends the fee description, amount, and internal reference numbers. Stripe collects payment details on its own pages and returns the payer’s name and email, card brand, last four digits, and its transaction record, which Program Partner stores with the payment. Full card numbers never reach Program Partner. When a program connects its account, Program Partner sends Stripe the program’s name, contact email, and internal organization ID; Stripe collects the program’s business, representative, and bank details on its own pages, and Program Partner keeps the Stripe account ID and checks its onboarding status.
Square
Payment processing on Square-hosted pages, using each participating program’s own Square account

Program Partner sends the fee description, amount, and an internal reference number. Square returns the cardholder’s name, buyer email, card brand, last four digits, and its transaction record, which Program Partner stores with the payment. Full card numbers never reach Program Partner. When a program connects its account, Program Partner stores Square’s authorization (encrypted) and the merchant and location IDs, and reads the business and location names to show which account is connected.
PayPal
Payment processing, including Venmo, on PayPal-hosted pages, using each participating program’s own PayPal account

Program Partner sends the fee description, amount, and an internal reference number. PayPal returns the payer’s name and email, the card brand and last four digits when a card is used, and its transaction record, which Program Partner stores with the payment. Full card numbers never reach Program Partner. When a program connects its account, Program Partner sends PayPal the program’s contact email and an internal connection ID; PayPal collects the rest on its own pages and returns the seller ID, which Program Partner keeps, and Program Partner checks the account’s onboarding status.
Google
Google sign-in; read-only import of a Google Calendar a program connects; optional storage of Skill Pathways recordings in a program’s own Google Drive
Google account identity information; events from the connected calendar; recordings, only when a program connects Google Drive
Microsoft
Read-only import of an Outlook calendar a program connects
Events from the connected calendar, and the settings needed to keep it in sync
Apple, Google, Microsoft, and Mozilla push services
Delivery of notifications to devices and browsers where a user turns them on

A device push address and an encrypted notification the push service cannot read. The notification holds a generic notice, a link within the app, and internal reference numbers; no names, message content, or other student information.
Cloudflare R2
Stores a daily backup of the database and uploaded files, separate from Supabase
The full database and uploaded files, encrypted before they leave the application with a key only Program Partner holds; the storage provider cannot read them
GitHub
Private source control and deployment workflow; checks that backups exist; hosts the myprogrampartner.com website (GitHub Pages)

Source code, deployment metadata, and development notes. Program Partner keeps details about individual users out of development notes and checks them automatically for email addresses, phone numbers, and record identifiers. For website visitors, the IP address and request details of each page request.

segs.text: No advertising network is integrated into the Services. Program Partner will update this list before enabling any new service that materially processes school-controlled or child information.

The app runs on Cloudflare’s network, and its database, sign-ins, and files are kept in a Supabase project that Lovable manages for Program Partner (Lovable Cloud). Supabase states that a project’s database, sign-in service, and stored files stay in the region selected for the project. Network, email, payment, sign-in, support, and operational metadata handled by other providers may be processed in other locations described in their terms and documentation.

Lovable Cloud keeps its own daily backups of the database for a short period. Program Partner’s daily encrypted backup of the database and uploaded files is stored in Cloudflare R2, separately from Supabase, and can be read only with a key Program Partner holds.

Program Partner uses administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards appropriate to the nature of the Services. Current controls include encrypted network connections, authenticated access, organization- and role-based authorization enforced by database rules and server checks, private storage for uploaded files, managed cloud infrastructure, access restrictions, and security and audit logging. Supabase encrypts stored data with AES-256 and data in transit with TLS. Credentials for services a program connects are additionally encrypted before they are stored, and daily backups of the database and uploaded files are encrypted before they leave the application. When Program Partner staff open a program to give support, the session is time-limited, its reason is recorded, and it is logged.
No online service can guarantee absolute security. Users should protect their credentials and report suspected unauthorized access to
support@myprogrampartner.com

If Program Partner becomes aware of a security incident affecting protected information, it will investigate, take reasonable containment and remediation measures, and notify affected organizations or individuals as required by law or applicable agreement.

School-controlled records are retained according to the participating organization’s instructions, the organization’s active use of the Services, documented backup cycles, and applicable law. Program Partner does not intend to retain child or student information indefinitely.

After a school or organization ends its use of Program Partner, school-controlled records will be returned if the organization asks and then deleted within 45 days of the organization’s written request or the end of its service, unless a shorter period is agreed or retention is required by law. Copies in encrypted backups expire within 30 days after that. If a backup is ever restored, previously deleted records are deleted again.

A user may request deletion of the user’s own account information by contacting support. Requests concerning school-controlled student records must be directed to the participating school or program, which will instruct Program Partner as appropriate. Deleting an account does not automatically require deletion of records the school must retain or records documenting completed transactions, submissions, permissions, or communications.

Users may request access to or correction of their own account information through available settings or by contacting support. Parents, guardians, eligible students, and others seeking school-controlled educational records should contact the participating organization. Authorized organizations may request an export, correction, return, or deletion of their controlled records, subject to applicable law and agreed procedures.

Users may manage browser permissions and unsubscribe from optional communications where offered. Required account, security, transactional, or school-authorized communications may still be sent. Organization administrators control many program communication settings and recipient selections.

The Services use essential cookies or comparable browser storage for sign-in, session continuity, security, organization selection, preferences, and core functionality. Email messages may use provider-hosted images or tracked links to report delivery or engagement where enabled. Program Partner does not use school-controlled student information for cross-site behavioral advertising. The myprogrampartner.com website sets no cookies (see section 12).

blocks.text: 12. Our website, demo requests, and messages to us

segs.text: This section covers myprogrampartner.com, which anyone can visit without an account. It does not cover the records programs keep in the app, which the sections above describe.
Visiting the site.

The site sets no cookies and carries no advertising trackers or social-media pixels. Cloudflare Web Analytics counts page views without cookies and without following you from site to site. Like any website host, GitHub, which serves the site, receives your IP address and browser details with each page request. Links to our Facebook and Instagram pages are plain links; those sites’ own policies apply once you follow one.
The Let’s chat form.

When you send a message, we collect what you enter: your name, email, role, school or studio, state, program type and size, the topics you want help with, the tools you use now, your message, your consent to be emailed about it, and the page you sent it from. It is stored in Program Partner’s own database, using the providers in section 6, and we receive an email notice of it through Resend. To limit spam, we also record your email address and IP address for repeated-submission checks, and delete those records after 7 days.
Scheduling a demo.
The Schedule a demo button takes you to the Let’s chat form, and we reply by email with times for a call.
How we use it.

We use what you send only to reply to you, prepare a demo or quote, and follow up on your request. We don’t sell it, share it for anyone else’s marketing, or add you to a mailing list unless you ask. We keep a message for as long as we’re in contact about it, and no more than 24 months after our last contact, and delete it sooner if you ask at
support@myprogrampartner.com
Children.
The website and its forms are for adults, such as directors, booster officers, and studio teachers. If we learn that a child under 13 has sent us a message, we delete it.
Woodshed.
Woodshed, our free practice site, has
its own privacy notice
. When a student opens practice that their Program assigned in Program Partner, Woodshed sends the results back to Program Partner, where they’re kept with that student’s records for the Program.

This policy may be updated as the Services, providers, data practices, or legal requirements change. The effective date will be revised when a new version is published. Material changes affecting school-controlled information will be communicated to participating organizations as required by agreement or law. Where required, Program Partner will obtain authorization before applying a materially different use to previously collected information.
Privacy, account-deletion, and security questions may be sent to
support@myprogrampartner.com
. A mailing address is available upon verified request. Requests involving school-controlled student records should first be directed to the participating school or program.

segs.text: These Terms of Service (the “Terms”) govern your use of the Program Partner app at app.myprogrampartner.com, the website at myprogrampartner.com, and related services (together, the “Services”), provided by Program Partner, LLC (“Program Partner,” “we,” “us”). By using the Services, you agree to these Terms. If you accept them for a school, college, booster organization, studio or other group, you confirm that you have authority to bind it.

items.text: Programs.

A school or college program, booster organization, private studio or other group that uses Program Partner under a quote or order form (a “Program”). The order form and these Terms make up the agreement between the Program and Program Partner. If the Program signs a separate agreement with us, such as a student data privacy agreement, that signed agreement controls where it conflicts with these Terms.
Authorized users.
Directors, staff, booster officers, parents and guardians, students and others a Program gives access to.
Visitors.
Anyone who browses myprogrampartner.com or sends us a message from it.
No self-signup.
We set up each Program by hand. The Program then creates accounts for its staff, families and students, using invitations or join codes.
The Program controls access.
The Program decides who has an account, which role each person holds, and what each role can see. It removes access when someone leaves.
Your sign-in.
Keep your password and sign-in details private. You are responsible for what happens under your account. Tell us right away at
support@myprogrampartner.com
if you think someone else has used it.
Students.
Students use Program Partner only through a Program that gives them access. For a student under 13, a school gives consent on the parent’s behalf for school purposes, as our Privacy Policy explains.
Demo access.
Demo schools are fictional and are for evaluating Program Partner. Demo access is by invitation, can be ended at any time, and must not be used to store real student or family information.

blocks.text: 3. What the Program is responsible for

segs.text: The Program:

items.text: has the right to provide the information it puts into Program Partner, and gives any notices and gets any consents the law or its own policies require, including notices under FERPA;
keeps its information accurate, and reviews the balances, fees, forms and records it relies on;
chooses which features to turn on and how to set them up;
follows the laws and policies that apply to it, including its district’s rules on student records and communications;
is responsible for the messages its users send through Program Partner; and
does not store Social Security numbers, full payment card numbers, bank account numbers or passwords for other services in ordinary fields, notes, forms or messages.

segs.text: A Program’s records belong to the Program. We use them only to provide and support the Services for that Program, as described in our Privacy Policy and in any data privacy agreement we sign with the Program. We never sell student or family information, never use it for advertising, and the Services never send school records to artificial-intelligence services.

blocks.text: 5. Payments families make to a Program

items.text: Into the Program’s own account.

A Program that takes online payments connects its own Stripe, Square or PayPal account. Payments go straight to that account. Program Partner never receives, holds or controls the Program’s funds, and charges no fee on payments.
The processor’s terms apply.

The Program’s agreement with its processor governs its account, including the processor’s standard rates, payouts and holds. The Program accepts that agreement when it connects the account. We are not a party to it.
The Program is the seller.
The Program sets its fees and is responsible for refunds, disputes and chargebacks, taxes, and any receipts or tax letters its donors and families need.
Families.
Questions about a fee, a refund or a balance go to the Program. Program Partner can’t change what a Program charges or give refunds on its behalf.
Balances.
Program Partner posts payments to balances automatically where it can. If a balance looks wrong, the Program should check it in the app and tell us if the app made the mistake.

segs.text: We quote each Program. The quote or order form sets the fees, the service period and how we invoice. Guided setup is included. Data import, if the Program asks us to do it, is quoted separately. Invoices are due within 30 days. Fees don’t include taxes unless the order form says so. If an invoice goes unpaid, we’ll give written notice and at least 15 days to pay before we suspend access. Families never pay Program Partner to use the app.
You may not:

items.text: use the Services to break the law, or to harass, threaten or harm anyone;
try to see another Program’s records or another person’s account, or get around a permission, limit or security control;
upload malware, or test the Services for security weaknesses without our written permission (if you find a weakness, please report it to
support@myprogrampartner.com
connect AI assistants, bots, scrapers or other automated tools to an account, or copy data out of the Services except through the exports they offer;
copy, resell or rent the Services, or reverse engineer them except where the law allows it;
send spam or messages people didn’t agree to receive; or
upload content you don’t have the right to share.

segs.text: You and your Program keep ownership of what you add, such as rosters, forms, documents, scores, parts, recordings and messages. You give us permission to host, copy, process and show that content only as needed to provide the Services to your Program.

The Program is responsible for having the rights to what it shares. That includes copyrighted music, digital parts and recordings: sharing them only with the students who need them does not by itself give the Program the right to copy or share them. We may remove content that breaks these Terms or the law.
Copyright complaints.

To report content you believe infringes your copyright, send a notice to our designated agent under the Digital Millennium Copyright Act: James Stanley English, III, Program Partner, LLC, 8735 Dunwoody Place, Ste R, Atlanta, GA 30350; (478) 972-5806;
support@myprogrampartner.com

. Include the work, where it appears in Program Partner, your contact details, and the statements the Act requires. When we receive a valid notice, we remove or disable the material and tell the Program. We end the access of users who repeatedly infringe.

Program Partner’s software, design, name and logo belong to us. While your Program’s subscription is active, its authorized users may use the Services for the Program’s own purposes under these Terms. If you send us ideas or feedback, we may use them without owing you anything.

Some features rely on other companies’ services, such as Google sign-in, Google Calendar and Google Drive, Outlook calendars, and Stripe, Square and PayPal. Their own terms apply when you use them, and we are not responsible for them. If one of them changes or stops a service, the matching feature may change or stop too.

blocks.text: 11. Availability and changes to the Services

segs.text: We work to keep the Services running, but we can’t promise they will never be interrupted, including for maintenance. We add and change features over time. We won’t remove a core feature a Program relies on during a paid term without telling the Program first. We back up the database and uploaded files every day and keep those backups for 30 days, but a Program should still export the records it must keep.

items.text: A Program can stop using the Services as its order form allows.

We may suspend or end access for unpaid invoices (after the notice in section 6), for a serious or repeated breach of these Terms, or to protect the Services or other Programs. We’ll give notice first when we reasonably can.
A user’s access ends when the Program removes it.
The Program’s records afterward.

Directors can export records at any time. When a Program’s service ends, or it asks us in writing, we’ll send an export if asked and then delete its records within 45 days. Deletion starts after a 14-day hold, so a request made by mistake can be stopped. Parent and student logins that belong to no other Program are deleted with it. Copies in backups expire within 30 days after that.

segs.text: To the extent the law allows, the Services are provided “as is” and “as available,” without warranties of any kind beyond those in a Program’s signed agreement. Program Partner helps a Program keep its records; it does not replace the Program’s own bookkeeping, audits or legal duties, and it doesn’t give accounting, tax or legal advice.

To the extent the law allows: neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits; and Program Partner’s total liability for any claim about the Services is limited to the fees the Program paid us in the 12 months before the claim.

To the extent the law allows, a Program will cover claims by others arising from content it adds or from its unlawful use of the Services, and we will cover claims that the Services, as we provide them, infringe someone else’s intellectual property.

These Terms are governed by the laws of Georgia. If a dispute comes up, we’ll each try in good faith to settle it informally for 30 days first. If that fails, it goes to the state or federal courts in Georgia. If a Program is a public body that the law requires to use its own state’s law or courts, those apply instead.

We may update these Terms. We’ll post the new version here with a new effective date, and email each Program’s administrators at least 30 days before a material change takes effect. Continuing to use the Services after that means you accept the change. A signed agreement changes only in writing signed by both parties.

These Terms, the Program’s order form and any signed agreement are the whole agreement about the Services. If part of these Terms can’t be enforced, the rest still applies. Not enforcing a term isn’t a waiver of it. Neither party is responsible for delays caused by events outside its reasonable control. If Program Partner is merged or acquired, these Terms pass to the new owner, and data privacy agreements stay in force. Notices to us go to
support@myprogrampartner.com
; notices to a Program go to its administrators’ email addresses.
Questions about these Terms:
support@myprogrampartner.com

accessibility.title: Program Partner Accessibility Statement
accessibility.name: Accessibility

segs.text: We want every director, staff member, parent and student to be able to use Program Partner, including people who use a screen reader, a keyboard, magnification or voice control. Our goal is to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA, on our website and in the app.
Our website (myprogrampartner.com)

is built to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. Before it goes live, and after major changes, we check text contrast, keyboard use, visible focus, image descriptions, reduced motion, and layouts down to 360 pixels wide.
The app (app.myprogrampartner.com)
is working toward WCAG 2.1 AA. We haven’t completed a full audit against it, so we don’t claim full conformance yet. Today the app:

items.text: declares its language and marks up pages with headings and landmarks, so screen readers can move through them;
lets you zoom with your browser, and works at phone widths;
shows a visible outline on buttons, links and fields when you move through them with a keyboard;
announces many status messages, such as saving, to screen readers; and
runs in any current web browser, with nothing to install.
The app doesn’t yet have a “skip to main content” link.

Documents, scores, parts and recordings a program uploads are only as accessible as the files themselves. A scanned PDF, for example, may not work with a screen reader. Ask your director for another format.

Some steps happen on pages other companies run: Google sign-in and the Stripe, Square and PayPal payment pages. We can’t fix those pages ourselves, but we’ll report problems to them and help you finish another way.

blocks.text: If something doesn’t work for you

segs.text: Email
support@myprogrampartner.com
. Tell us the page or screen, what you were trying to do, and your device, browser and any assistive technology. We reply within one business day.

If a barrier stops you from finishing something, such as paying a fee, signing a form or reading a message, we’ll help you finish it another way, working with your director when needed. Families can also ask their director to take a payment by cash or check, or to provide a form in another format. We’ll tell you when the problem is fixed.
If you are reviewing Program Partner for your district, email
support@myprogrampartner.com
for details of our accessibility work.
